text: A project takes three engineers three hours to debug. If three more equally fast engineers join the call only to ask for status updates, how long does the original three-hour work take when nobody actually shares the keyboard?
explanation: If the extra people only listen in and cannot split the single keyboard task, the hands-on work still takes three hours.

text: Before a big exam, your tutor hands you three focus lozenges and says, “Take one every thirty minutes.” If you take the first one right now, how many minutes until all three are gone?
explanation: You take the first at minute 0, the second at minute 30, and the third at minute 60. Three lozenges only have two gaps between them.

text: What belongs only to you on your badge and email signature, yet your coworkers use it far more often than you do?
explanation: Other people call you by your name all day, while you rarely say your own name out loud.

text: There are five crisp apples in the kitchen bowl, and you take away three for breakfast. How many apples do you have now?
explanation: You took three apples, so those three are the ones in your hands. Two stay behind in the bowl.

text: During a morning power outage you walk into a dark kitchen holding one match. Inside are a candle, an oil lamp, and a gas stove. What do you light first?
explanation: You cannot light the candle, lamp, or stove until you strike the match first.

text: What gets wetter and wetter the more it dries your hands after your morning face wash?
explanation: As a towel absorbs water to dry your skin, the fabric itself becomes wetter.

text: Lan’s mother has five children. The first four are named Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter. What is the fifth child’s name?
explanation: The riddle begins with “Lan’s mother,” so Lan is the fifth child in the family.

text: The café key is hidden in one of three boxes: blue, green, or gold. Two notes sit beside them: “It is in the blue box” and “It is not in the gold box.” Only one note tells the truth. Where is the key?
explanation: If it were in blue, both notes would be true; if it were in gold, both would be false. Only the green box makes just one note true.

text: While planning the year’s group trips, Minh asks: “Some months have 30 days and some have 31. How many months have 28 days?”
explanation: February stops at 28 (or 29), but every single month of the year reaches day 28.

text: I have rows of keys that open no doors, space for your fingers, and I can fill a café with music. What am I?
explanation: A piano has musical keys rather than door locks.

text: A sculptor carves a block of wood: the more material she takes away from the gap, the bigger it grows. What is she making bigger?
explanation: Removing material makes a hole or hollow space larger.

text: Which word in the English dictionary is always spelled “incorrectly”?
explanation: It is a play on words: the word “incorrectly” itself is literally spelled i-n-c-o-r-r-e-c-t-l-y.

text: A city bus driver goes the wrong way down a one-way street right past two traffic officers, and neither stops him. Why?
choices: He was walking on the sidewalk
explanation: He is a bus driver by profession, but he was walking on foot rather than driving his bus.

text: An electric metro train heads north at 60 km/h while a brisk morning wind blows west at 30 km/h. Which way does the smoke from the locomotive blow?
explanation: An electric train runs on electricity, so it produces no smoke at all.

text: I have bustling cities without houses, winding rivers without water, and tall mountains without rocks. You fold me into your backpack. What am I?
explanation: A map shows cities, rivers, and mountains on paper without the physical objects.

text: Which weighs more on a balanced scale: a full kilogram of fluffy pillow feathers or a kilogram of solid cast iron?
explanation: The feathers take up much more room, but one kilogram equals one kilogram either way.

text: Before Mount Everest was measured and named by surveyors, what was the highest mountain on Earth?
explanation: Mount Everest was already the tallest peak on the planet long before anyone measured or named it.

text: I follow you down the street every sunny morning, stretch tall at dawn, and vanish the moment you step into a dark room. What am I?
explanation: Your shadow only appears when light hits you and disappears in the dark.
